items.title: $400,000 in Dividend Stocks: How a Roth IRA Could Save You $3,780 a Year
items.summary: The highest-yielding stock in this six-stock dividend portfolio is not the one costing you the most at tax time. Find out which holding triggers the biggest bill, and why where you park it matters more than what it pays.

items.title: 3 Monthly Dividend Stocks That Could Help Pay Your Retirement Bills
items.summary: Your bills show up every month, but most dividend checks only arrive four times a year. Three monthly payers promise to close that gap, though one of them carries a hidden catch that could shrink part of the paycheck.

items.title: 4 High-Yield Dividend Stocks You Can Buy Today and Hold Forever
items.summary: Four stocks yielding close to 6% each have rallied hard in 2026, yet income investors keep holding on. Before you buy, one carries a 78% payout with missing cash flow data and another sits at 1.42x interest coverage, so knowing which is truly built to last matters.

items.title: Want Reliable Dividend Income? These 4 High-Yield Stocks Have Balance Sheets Lenders Still Trust
items.summary: When a dividend gets cut, lenders usually see trouble first. Four payers yielding above 5% span telecom, tobacco, real estate, and logistics, yet one of them runs a coverage cushion so thin that a weak peak season could test it.

items.title: Benjamin Graham Had a 20-Year Rule for Retirement Income. It Just Won the AI Sell-Off
items.summary: Benjamin Graham's rule for the defensive investor was uninterrupted dividends for at least 20 years. In the month since the S&P 500's record, five holdings that pass it rose 8.8% while the Nasdaq-100 fund fell 13.6%. Here is what that did to a retired couple with $3 million living on $99,265 a year of dividends, and three moves for the week.

items.title: 3 Dividend Aristocrats Yielding More Than the 2027 COLA
items.summary: Social Security just promised retirees a raise, but three blue-chip payers have been handing out bigger starting checks and annual bumps for decades. One pays monthly, one holds a record no other REIT can touch, and one carries a warning sign.

items.title: A 70-Year-Old Swapped O for ADC in a $1.03 Million Income Portfolio. Here’s What Happened to Her $5,650 Monthly Paycheck
items.summary: Two monthly-paying REITs look nearly identical on paper, yet one retiree is betting her income on swapping a giant for a smaller rival. What does she gain, what does she give up, and does her paycheck survive?
